q-182446.name: Question 1
q-182446.problem:
$\,$ $P$ is not a rhombus and $Q$ is not a rectangle.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
q-182446.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,¬(P\text{ is not a rhombus}\text{ and }Q\text{ is not a rectangle}) & ≡¬((P\text{ is not a rhombus})∧(Q\text{ is not a rectangle})) \\  & ≡¬(P\text{ is not a rhombus})∨¬(Q\text{ is not a rectangle}) \\  & ≡(P\text{ is a rhombus})∨(Q\text{ is a rectangle}) \\  & ≡P\text{ is a rhombus}\text{ or }Q\text{ is a rectangle}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

P is not a rhombus or Q is a rectangle.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a
P is a rhombus or Q is not a rectangle
b
P is a rhombus and Q is not a rectangle
c
P is a rhombus or Q is a rectangle
d
P is not a rhombus or Q is not a rectangle
e
P is a rhombus and Q is a rectangle
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B.

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(P is not a rhombus or Q is a rectangle)≡¬((P is not a rhombus)∨(Q is a rectangle))≡¬(P is not a rhombus)∧¬(Q is a rectangle)≡(P is a rhombus)∧(Q is not a rectangle)≡P is a rhombus and Q is not a rectangle.

Question 8
?

3|18 or 11 is not prime.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

c

d

e

Submit
Incorrect

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B.

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(3|18 or 11 is not prime)≡¬((3|18)∨(11 is not prime))≡¬(3|18)∧¬(11 is not prime)≡(3⧸|18)∧(11 is prime)≡3⧸|18 and 11 is prime.

q-182619.html:
Question 10
?

0 is negative or {0} is not empty.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a
0 is not negative and {0} is not empty
b
0 is not negative or {0} is empty
c
0 is not negative and {0} is empty
d
0 is negative and {0} is empty
e
0 is negative or {0} is not empty
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B.

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(0 is negative or {0} is not empty)≡¬((0 is negative)∨({0} is not empty))≡¬(0 is negative)∧¬({0} is not empty)≡(0 is not negative)∧({0} is empty)≡0 is not negative and {0} is empty.
q-182619.knowledge_point: Negating a Sentence Containing a Disjunction

q-1485.name: Question 11
q-1485.problem: Simplify the statement $¬((Q∧P)∨R)$ using De Morgan's laws.
q-1485.worked_solution:
De Morgan's laws state that

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(Q∧P)≡¬P∨¬R, \\ ¬(Q∨P)≡¬P∧¬Q.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬((Q∧P)∨R) & ≡¬(Q∧P)∧¬R \\  & ≡(¬Q∨¬P)∧¬R\end{aligned}
$$
